typeName: BC techniques: parts, improper integrals, Euler, arc length
title: Euler's method, concavity and arc length

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Use Euler's method, starting at x=0x = 0 with two steps of equal size, to approximate f(1)f(1). Show the work that leads to your answer in a table with columns xx, yy, dydx\frac{dy}{dx} and Δx\Delta x.

rubric.point: First step: slope <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0, 1)</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(0.5)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 1 + (-1)(0.5)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 0.5</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: the first row of a labeled table: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = -1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta x = 0.5</annotation></semantics></math>

rubric.point: Second step uses the slope at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0.5, 0.5)</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2(0.5) - 0.5 = 0.5</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.5</mn><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5 + (0.5)(0.5)</annotation></semantics></math> written unsimplified

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>, or any unsimplified form such as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 + (-1)(0.5) + (0.5)(0.5)</annotation></semantics></math>
no answer point for a third step or a step size other than 0.5

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta x = 0.5</annotation></semantics></math>. Table: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = 2(0) - 1 = -1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta y = -0.5</annotation></semantics></math>; <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0.5</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 0.5</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2(0.5) - 0.5</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 0.5</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta y = 0.25</annotation></semantics></math>; <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.75</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 0.75</annotation></semantics></math>. So <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.75</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(1) \approx 0.75</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find d2ydx2\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} in terms of xx and yy. The first step in part (a) gives f(0.5)≈0.5f(0.5) \approx 0.5. Is this an overestimate or an underestimate of f(0.5)f(0.5)? Explain your reasoning.

rubric.point: Underestimate, with reason: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= f(x) - (2x - 2) > 0</annotation></semantics></math>, so the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is concave up and lies above its tangent line at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>, which the first step follows
accept: "<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">″</mo></mrow><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'' > 0</annotation></semantics></math> on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 0.5]</annotation></semantics></math> because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>></mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) > 2x - 2</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is concave up and the tangent line approximation is too small"

no point for "underestimate" without the concavity reason, or with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> increasing as the reason

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{d}{dx}(2x - y)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2 - \frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2 - (2x - y)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2 - 2x</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ y</annotation></semantics></math>. On the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= f(x) - (2x - 2) > 0</annotation></semantics></math> because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>></mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) > 2x - 2</annotation></semantics></math>. So the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is concave up, and it lies above its tangent line at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>. The first Euler step follows that tangent line, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math> is an underestimate of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(0.5)</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Write, but do not evaluate, an integral expression in terms of xx and f(x)f(x) that gives the length of the graph of ff from x=0x = 0 to x=1x = 1.

rubric.point: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><msqrt><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^1 \sqrt{1 + \left(2x - f(x)\right)^2}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><msqrt><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^1 \sqrt{1 + (f'(x))^2}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(x) = 2x - f(x)</annotation></semantics></math> stated
no point if the square root, the square or the 1 is missing, or the limits are wrong

parts.sample: Since <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(x) = 2x - f(x)</annotation></semantics></math>, the length is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><msqrt><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^1 \sqrt{1 + \left(2x - f(x)\right)^2}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: A different curve is the graph of g(x)=x33+14xg(x) = \frac{x^3}{3} + \frac{1}{4x} for 1≤x≤21 \le x \le 2. Find the length of this curve. Show the work that leads to your answer.

accept: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g'(x) = x^2 - \frac{1}{4x^2}</annotation></semantics></math> placed correctly in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><msqrt><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_1^2 \sqrt{1 + (g'(x))^2}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>

rubric.point: Simplified integrand: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 + \left(x^2 - \frac{1}{4x^2}\right)^2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \left(x^2 + \frac{1}{4x^2}\right)^2</annotation></semantics></math>, so the integrand is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2 + \frac{1}{4x^2}</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>16</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^4 + \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{16x^4}</annotation></semantics></math> recognized as a perfect square

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><msubsup><mo stretchy="true" symmetric="true" minsize="1.8em" maxsize="1.8em">|</mo><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\frac{x^3}{3} - \frac{1}{4x}\right)\Big|_1^2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \left(\frac{8}{3} - \frac{1}{8}\right) - \left(\frac{1}{3} - \frac{1}{4}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> or any equivalent
